subject: Engineer / Technical Officer, Road Design (East), reference 12067, Marc Masarate
email_body:
Dear Vincent,

I'm preparing an application for the Engineer / Technical Officer, Road Design (East) position (reference 12067) and have two questions before I submit, since the advert names you for further information.

The position description gives Sunshine or Ringwood as the usual place of work. Is the East team based at Ringwood, or would Sunshine be an option? And would a candidate trained on AutoCAD and Civil 3D, who has not used MicroStation or OpenRoads yet, be considered for the VPS 3 role?

For context: an Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design finished in February 2026 (road geometry, earthworks, pavement and stormwater drainage to Australian Standards and Austroads guides), a civil engineering degree (Philippines, 2019), and eleven months on site. I'm based in Melton. My drawings are at https://macdarenz-droid.github.io/Portfolio.

Kind regards,
Marc Darenz Masarate
0478 764 077
https://macdarenz-droid.github.io/Portfolio

letter.subject: Application for Engineer / Technical Officer, Road Design (East), VPS 3
paragraphs: I'm applying for the Engineer / Technical Officer, Road Design (East) position advertised on Careers Vic. Road geometry, earthworks, pavement and drainage design to Austroads guides is what my Australian diploma covered; intersections, roadside safety and the DTP supplements would be new to me, and a supervised VPS 3 road design role is the kind of start I'm after. The paragraphs below follow the selection criteria.

Foundational engineering knowledge, applied professionally: my Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (Philippines, 2019) is the mandatory civil qualification, and in February 2026 I completed an Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design at the Albright Institute of Business and Language. There I designed and documented road geometry, earthworks, pavement and stormwater drainage in AutoCAD and Civil 3D to Australian Standards and Austroads guides, applied AS 1742.14, AS 1726 and AS 1289, kept risk registers, and lodged Before You Dig Australia enquiries so designs fitted around existing services.

Adaptable and technically capable: my AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Revit skills all come from study, I have not used MicroStation or OpenRoads yet, and I would pick up the Bentley tools the same way I picked up Civil 3D. Delivering work and keeping records: on site in the Philippines from April 2019 to February 2020 I planned each day's priorities for 10 to 15 workers, tracked procurement and materials, and kept site reports, material records and progress reports.

Working collaboratively and applying sound judgement: on those sites I coordinated with engineers, subcontractors, suppliers and clients, checked work against the drawings and project requirements, and escalated issues that needed clarification or corrective action. I hold a White Card, an Australian driver's licence with my own transport, and full working rights until December 2027 on a Subclass 485 visa; I'm based in Melton and can travel within Victoria for site inspections.

My resume is attached and my drawings, including a two-lane road cross-section with kerbs and drainage, are at https://macdarenz-droid.github.io/Portfolio. I'd welcome a conversation about the team's projects.

screening_answers.question: Works collaboratively, sharing information, supporting colleagues and contributing positively to team goals.
screening_answers.answer: On site in the Philippines (April 2019 to February 2020) I coordinated 10 to 15 workers a day, passed on work priorities, coordinated with engineers, subcontractors and suppliers to sort out site issues, and kept clients and stakeholders up to date on progress.

screening_answers.question: Delivers work effectively, prioritising tasks by urgency and impact, working to agreed plans and maintaining accurate project records.
screening_answers.answer: As project-in-charge on a community hall renovation I tracked progress against a six-month construction program and it finished on time; as a field engineer I tracked procurement and materials and prepared site reports, material records and progress reports on a three-month schedule.

screening_answers.question: Applies sound judgement and problem-solving skills, using established policies and processes and seeking guidance when needed.
screening_answers.answer: I reviewed structural and architectural drawings, checked work against project requirements, and escalated issues that needed clarification or corrective action to the engineers. In the diploma I did options analyses and kept risk registers.

screening_answers.question: Applies foundational engineering knowledge professionally, using relevant standards, guidelines, codes and risk controls to develop and document practical engineering solutions.
screening_answers.answer: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (2019) and Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design (February 2026): road geometry, earthworks, pavement and stormwater drainage designed and documented in AutoCAD and Civil 3D to Australian Standards and Austroads guides, with AS 1742.14, AS 1726, AS 1289 and risk registers applied in coursework.

screening_answers.question: Adaptable and technically capable, open to new approaches and developing skills in road and traffic engineering, roadside safety, and CAD tools including MicroStation and OpenRoads.
screening_answers.answer: My AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Revit skills all come from study; I have not used MicroStation or OpenRoads yet and would pick up the Bentley tools the same way, alongside the road and traffic engineering and roadside safety work the team does.

screening_answers.question: Victorian Driver's License (required).
screening_answers.answer: [Marc to confirm: an Australian driver's licence is on record; the state is not.]

screening_answers.question: Ability to travel within the state for site inspections (required).

checklist: Confirm your driver's licence is Victorian (the ad requires it) before applying. If it is not, do not apply until it is transferred.

Optional, before applying: send the prepared email to Vincent Nguyen (the advert names him for further information) to ask whether the East team sits at Ringwood or Sunshine and whether AutoCAD and Civil 3D training is acceptable. Use the Send from Gmail button on this record.
The letter says a supervised VPS 3 road design role is the start you are after; change that line if it is not true for you.
Open https://www.careers.vic.gov.au/job/engineer-technical-officer-road-design-east-88237 and press Apply (reference 12067); you may need to create an account on the DTP recruitment platform.

Attach the two PDFs from this record (resume and cover letter). The cover letter already addresses each key selection criterion; if the portal asks for criterion responses separately, paste the screening answers above.
Submit before 11:59 pm Tuesday 6 October 2026. Email and manual submissions are not accepted.
Press Applied on the tracker with the date and "Company website".
notes: Victorian Government entry-level road design role (VPS 3, ongoing) in Melbourne, found on Careers Vic by the browser sweep, not on SEEK. Position description read: mandatory civil qualification (met), Austroads road design knowledge desirable (coursework), Bentley software desirable (not used, disclosed). Visa holders are eligible. The senior manager's email is printed on the advert for further information; the prepared email is a genuine enquiry (place of work, CAD training) Marc can send before applying. The position description gives Sunshine or Ringwood as the usual place of work; Sunshine is much closer to Melton.
